title: Prosper
summary: PROS'PER, verb transitive [Latin prospero, from prosperus, from the Gr. to carry to or toward; to bear.] To favor; to render successful. All things concur to prosper our design. PROS'PER, verb intrans

inlines.v: PROS'PER, verb transitive [Latin prospero, from prosperus, from the Gr. to carry to or toward; to bear.] To favor; to render successful. All things concur to prosper our design. PROS'PER, verb intransitive To be successful; to succeed. The Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hand. Genesis 39:3. He that covereth his sins, shall not prosper Proverbs 28:13. 1. To grow or increase; to thrive; to make gain; as, to prosper in business. Our agriculture, commerce and manufactures now prosper
